key_insight: A geometrically exact planar beam model can incorporate hyperelasticity consistently by separating cross-sectional deformation assumptions from constitutive reduction, with plane stress giving robust global behavior and plane strain introducing stronger Poisson-ratio sensitivity.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical beam formulation for simulating large-deformation structural members more accurately without resorting to full 3D solid analysis.
method: Start from a conventional three-field geometrically exact planar beam formulation.
Enrich the kinematics with a global in-plane thickness deformation field.
Treat out-of-plane behavior independently using plane-stress or plane-strain constitutive reductions for hyperelastic laws.
evidence_signal: Benchmark results in the abstract show plane stress gives nearly coincident centreline deformations across Poisson ratios, while plane strain becomes noticeably stiffer as Poisson's ratio increases; Saint Venant-Kirchhoff and Neo-Hookean models agree closely except for local out-of-plane stretch.
watch_item: Plane-strain reductions can over-stiffen the beam at higher Poisson ratios, so the constitutive assumption must be chosen carefully for the intended application.
paper_title: On finite elements for geometrically-exact planar beams with hyperelastic material models
